newsitem.title: JAPAN: GE unit in dispute with Japan tax bureau.
newsitem.headline: GE unit in dispute with Japan tax bureau.

text.p: General Electric International Inc, a wholly owned unit of General Electric Co, said on Tuesday that it has been hit with financial penalties by Japanese tax authorities related to income earned in Japan.

A spokeswoman at the U.S. unit's Japanese branch declined to provide figures, but the Kyodo news agency said the Tokyo Regional Taxation Bureau imposed about two billion yen in penalties and back-taxes on unreported income of about five billion yen in the two-year period to December 1995.
She added that the company had filed an objection with the bureau stating that the income had already been taxed in the United States.
"We have paid the income tax to U.S. tax authorities in accordance with our interpretation of the bilateral tax treaty between the U.S. and Japan," said the spokeswoman.
James Pomeroy, U.S.-based international communications manager for General Electric Co, said: "The issue is caused by a different interpretation of the (tax) treaty."
"We're leaving it up to the authorities in the Japanese and U.S. governments to help us determine what's right and what's wrong," Pomeroy said.
The GE unit's business in Japan includes researching the market, supplying GE products and seeking business partners for the GE group, the spokeswoman said.
